title: String Operations and Input
learningObjectives: Describe relevant storage, indexing and size rules.
Trace a collection operation or traversal.
Recognize bounds, lifetime or input pitfalls.
Apply the type to a practical collection task.

understand.concept: Text input and operations include token extraction, getline, concatenation, comparison and searching. cin stops at whitespace; getline reads spaces.
understand.whyItMatters: Text processing is common in interactive applications.
understand.explain: Choose the input method, handle leftover newlines and check npos from searches.

examples.title: Check empty
examples.explanation: empty checks whether the string contains no characters.

examples.title: Search substring
examples.explanation: find returns a position or std::string::npos.

examples.title: Prepare getline after cin
examples.explanation: Consume the leftover newline; include limits.

practise.guidedTask: Trace all five String Operations and Input examples. Record sizes, indexes, values and condition checks. Identify first/last valid element and relevant edge cases.
practise.independentTask: Create a small C++ data-processing program demonstrating string operations and input. Test typical values, empty/boundary cases, and invalid input or indexing where relevant. Explain why this collection is appropriate.
hints: Use zero-based indexes and verify bounds.
Prefer range-based traversal when index is unnecessary.
Check emptiness before operations such as front or pop_back.
Test first, last and invalid boundaries.
